source_ref: van Teffelen MW, Lobbestael J, Voncken MJ, Peeters F (2020) PLoS ONE 15(10):e0239631, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0239631 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 Data .sav (journal.pone.0239631.s001), variable labels + value labels for HOS_1..HOS_8; English items from Buss AH & Perry M (1992) J Pers Soc Psychol 63:452-459, AQ hostility items 3/7/10/15/17/20/24/26
note: Level-1 extraction: item_text and option_text are the source .sav's own variable labels and value labels, transcribed verbatim (PLOS S1 Data, journal.pone.0239631.s001; SPSS, N=376). The IRW item codes HOS_1..HOS_8 ARE that file's column names -- data/vanteffelen_2020_hostility.py melts columns matching 'HOS_' with no rename -- so no positional or order inference was made. Instrument check (Step 3b): the eight Dutch labels are one-for-one the eight Buss & Perry (1992) AQ hostility items (nos. 3, 7, 10, 15, 17, 20, 24, 26 of the 29-item AQ), in a permuted administration order (HOS_1=#10 suspicious of overly friendly strangers, HOS_2=#20 laughing behind my back, HOS_3=#15 eaten up with jealousy, HOS_4=#24 other people get the breaks, HOS_5=#26 'friends' talk behind my back, HOS_6=#3 when people are especially nice, HOS_7=#17 raw deal out of life, HOS_8=#7 why so bitter) -- so the table name is correct. DISCREPANCY WITH THE PAPER: the Materials section calls it 'the 10-item hostility scale of the Aggression Questionnaire (AQH)' and describes a 5-point scale 'ranging from one (extremely uncharacteristic of me) to five (extremely characteristic of me)'. The deposit has 8 items (the canonical subscale length) and its value labels are an agreement scale: 1 Helemaal mee oneens, 2 Tamelijk mee oneens, 3 Weet niet, 4 Tamelijk mee eens, 5 Helemaal mee eens. The deposit was followed on both counts; '10-item' looks like a slip carried over from the sibling 10-item STAXI-2T and PID-5H scales described in the same paragraph. Note the midpoint is labelled 'Weet niet' (don't know) rather than a neutral agreement anchor -- that is what the file says. Scale direction agrees between the two sources (1 = least hostile, 5 = most), and all 8 items are positively keyed with no reverse items, so no keying override was needed. instructions and section_prompt left blank: the .sav carries no instruction string for the HOS block (it does for RPQ_1..RPQ_22, so their absence here is a fact about the file, not an oversight), and the only instruction text available is Buss & Perry's English, which describes the uncharacteristic/characteristic anchoring that was NOT administered here. Per-item n = 376 for all 8 items with no missing values, and every item uses all five levels (e.g. HOS_1: 60/111/42/143/20; HOS_3: 166/110/30/60/10). Translation: item_text_translated is Buss & Perry's own published English for the same eight items (official_instrument_english), not a translation of the Dutch string, so a local rewording would not show up there; option_text_translated is an IRW rendering of the Dutch anchors, since no official English exists for this Dutch agree/disagree anchor set. Hence translation_source=mixed. The Dutch is most plausibly Meesters, Muris, Bosma & Schouten (1996, Behav Res Ther 34:839-843), which the paper lists as reference 43, but the Materials section does not say so outright, so the shipped instrument field says 'Dutch administration' rather than naming that version. RIGHTS: not blocked. The itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv 'Autism Spectrum Quotient' row explicitly records that this table is the Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire and is NOT covered by the ARC AQ block (its codes are HOS_n, and it matches that row only by table name). No reserved right was locatable for the Buss & Perry AQ itself: it was published in a JPSP article rather than by a test publisher (the commercially sold WPS 'Aggression Questionnaire' is the different 34-item Buss & Warren 2000 instrument), and the PhenX Toolkit protocol for it (https://www.phenxtoolkit.org/protocols/view/640701) states 'This protocol is freely available; permission not required for use.' Silence is permission, so it was extracted normally. No register row was written: this is a ship-shaped finding, and a round may only write 'block' rows.
public_note: The paper's Materials section describes this scale as having 10 items anchored 'extremely uncharacteristic of me' to 'extremely characteristic of me', but the deposited data has the 8 canonical Buss-Perry hostility items and its own value labels are a Dutch agreement scale with a 'Weet niet' (don't know) midpoint; the item and option text shipped here follow the deposit, and the English of the response options was written by IRW rather than by the study.

note: mapping_basis=data_labels and the exemption is earned by the CODE DERIVATION, not just the label: data/vanteffelen_2020_hostility.py selects [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('AGG_')] and melts them with var_name='item', so the live item code IS the .sav column name -- no rename, no positional assignment. All 40 AGG_* columns of S1 Data carry a Dutch variable label, and the 40 shipped item_text strings were byte-compared against those labels: 40/40 identical, 0 mismatches. option_text/resp come from the same file's value labels, which are identical for all 40 AGG columns (1='(Bijna) nooit', 2='Zelden', 3='Soms', 4='Vaak', 5='(Bijna) altijd'); the script does pd.to_numeric on the raw SPSS codes and applies no recode, so the stored integers are those codes. Direction corroborated on the source file's own item means (n=376, complete for all 40 items): the five lowest are AGG_13 arson 1.02, AGG_26 destroying someone's house/things 1.03, AGG_34 pinning someone to the ground 1.03, AGG_33 damaging property 1.03, AGG_30 beating someone up 1.04, and the five highest are AGG_17 contradicting someone 2.88, AGG_21 being sarcastic 2.57, AGG_20 trying to have the last word 2.27, AGG_35 criticizing judgments 2.00, AGG_14 gossiping 1.83 -- severe physical/property acts at the floor and mild verbal/passive ones highest, which is only consistent with 1=(almost) never rather than a reversed reading. Step 3b: 'foa' is the Forms of Aggression questionnaire (Verona, Sadeh, Case, Reed & Bhattacharjee 2008, Assessment 15:493-510); the paper's Measures section names it, gives 40 items on a 1 ((almost) never) to 5 ((almost) always) scale and quotes one English example per subscale, all of which match AGG items here (AGG_4 'Slaan, schoppen of duwen' / 'I hit, kick, or push them'; AGG_7 'Gemene dingen tegen Iemand zeggen' / 'I say mean things to them'; AGG_33 'Schade toe brengen aan iemands bezittingen' / 'I damage their property'; AGG_8 / 'I ruin their friendships with other people'; AGG_19 'Kritiek leveren op iemands werk, zelfs als dat goed is' / 'I criticize their work, even if it is good'). Transcribed verbatim including the source's own artifacts: AGG_7 capitalises 'Iemand' mid-sentence, AGG_33 writes 'toe brengen' as two words, AGG_32 uses curly quotes around 'problemen'. Not corrected. instructions left blank: the AGG variable labels carry no stem (unlike the RPQ block in the same file, whose labels prepend the full Dutch instruction), and neither the paper nor S1 Data prints the Dutch FOA instruction -- the paper only describes it in English prose ('participants in the current study were asked to indicate how often each behavior occurs in general' rather than the original's 'when angry'), which is a description, not the administered text, so nothing was invented. section_id is a single trivial section: the FOA's five subscales are scoring groups, not shared-context testlets, and no section_prompt text exists. English in the _translated columns was produced by this project from the Dutch (translation_source=machine_translation); the five items above happen to correspond to the original English the paper quotes, but the other 35 have no published English rendering in this deposit. Rights: no reserved right located. The FOA has no row in instrument_rights_register.csv; it is a research questionnaire published in a SAGE journal article with no separate rights or permissions page, and a search turned up no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause anywhere for it, so it ships under 'silence is permission'. The deposit itself is CC BY 4.0 (PLOS ONE S1 Data). Note that the nearby AQ-family block row in the register covers the Autism Spectrum Quotient and explicitly does NOT cover this study.
public_note: The Forms of Aggression questionnaire was administered in Dutch and item_text ships that Dutch verbatim from the study's own SPSS variable labels; the English in the _translated columns was produced by IRW, not by the authors.
